doc_name: Institute of Combinatorics and its Applications
text: The Institute of Combinatorics and its Applications (ICA) is an international scientific organization established in 1990 to enhance the visibility and influence of the combinatorial community. Based in Duluth, Minnesota, with its operational office at the University of Minnesota Duluth, the ICA sponsors conferences, publishes a bulletin, and awards several medals, including the Euler, Hall, Kirkman, and Stanton Medals. The organization has over 800 members from more than forty countries, with membership divided into three levels: Members (those without a Ph.D.), Associate Fellows (typically assistant professors who have earned a Ph.D. or have published extensively), and Fellows (established scholars, usually at the associate professor or higher rank). Members engage in diverse areas, including theoretical research, education, and practical applications such as statistical design, communications theory, cryptography, and computer security. While fellowship in the ICA is not highly selective, the ICA also recognizes "honorary fellows" who have made pre-eminent contributions to combinatorics or its applications; there are at most ten living honorary fellows at any time, with deceased honorary fellows including H. S. M. Coxeter, Paul Erdős, Haim Hanani, Bernhard Neumann, D. H. Lehmer, Leonard Carlitz, Robert Frucht, E. M. Wright, and Horst Sachs. Living honorary fellows include S. S. Shrikhande, C. R. Rao, G. J. Simmons, Vera Sós, Henry Gould, Carsten Thomassen, Neil Robertson, Cheryl Praeger, and R. M. Wilson. The ICA publishes the Bulletin of the ICA (ISSN 1183-1278), a triannual journal appearing in January, May, and September, consisting of 128 pages, which includes survey and research papers, member news, and conference reports. Since 2017, research articles in the Bulletin have been made available on an open access basis. The Euler Medal is awarded annually to a member still active in research for distinguished career contributions to combinatorics, named after Leonhard Euler. The Hall Medal, named after Marshall Hall, Jr., recognizes outstanding achievements by members under age 40. The Kirkman Medal, named after Thomas Kirkman, honors members within four years past their Ph.D. The medal winners from 2010 to 2015 were decided by the ICA Medals Committee between November 2016 and February 2017 after the ICA resumed full activities in March 2016. In 2016, the ICA established the Stanton Medal, named after Ralph Stanton, to recognize substantial and sustained contributions beyond research—such as advocacy, outreach, service, teaching, or mentoring—to the promotion of combinatorics. The Stanton Medal is awarded at most once per year, typically to a Fellow of the ICA. The current vice-presidents of the ICA are Charles Colbourn, Dalibor Froncek, and Anita Pasotti, and Sarah Heuss serves as Secretary.
